bull.probability_evidence: Bull case: TTM ROIC 19.8%/ROE 22.5%, 8.74% FCF yield, P/FCF 11.4x at the 15th percentile of its 5y range with 96.2% FCF conversion TTM, buybacks cutting shares 3.33% YoY, near-unlevered balance sheet (0.23x net debt/EBITDA, Altman Z 3.69, Piotroski 7) and low beta 0.37, with the FY21-25 fundamental decline read as cyclical not competitive (research/EOG/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Bull case; research/EOG/2026-10-08.md section 2).

target_price_12m.cite: research/EOG/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Decision JSON scenarios.bull.target_price_12m=158, basis: P/FCF re-rates from 11.4x to 5y median 12.5x on TTM FCF

target_band.cite: Half the spread between bull-case implied prices from three valuation anchors at TTM fundamentals: P/FCF re-rate to 5y median 12.5x = $158.13, P/E re-rate to 5y max 11.4x = $145.49, EV/EBITDA at its already-current 5y-max 5.5x = $144.21 (fact sheet 5y multiple ranges, research/EOG/factsheet-2026-10-08.md Valuation table); half-spread $6.96 / $158 target = 0.044.

base.probability_evidence: Base case: EOG already sits near the top of its own 5y P/E (92nd pct) and EV/EBITDA (75th pct) ranges, so the bear case argues the price already reflects mid-cycle commodity strength, while the bull case's upside depends on a further re-rating that has not yet happened; absent a catalyst, returns come only from buybacks/dividend on a flat multiple (research/EOG/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Bear case and Base scenario basis).

target_price_12m.cite: research/EOG/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Decision JSON scenarios.base.target_price_12m=145, basis: EV/EBITDA holds at 5.5x on roughly flat TTM EBITDA

target_band.cite: Base case holds each multiple at its current level (P/E 11.3x, P/FCF 11.4x, EV/EBITDA 5.5x; research/EOG/factsheet-2026-10-08.md Valuation table), so all three anchors imply ~$144.21 (today's price) with a computed half-spread of effectively $0 against the $145 target; a minimal 0.005 floor is used rather than claiming literally zero anchor disagreement.

bear.probability_evidence: Bear case: five-year fundamental deterioration (ROIC 20.7%→16.0%, FCF margin 25.0%→15.2% FY21-25), net debt/EBITDA rising from -0.10x to 0.49x in FY2025, TTM results flattered by strong oil prices as a high-water mark, the macro overlay's small bear tilt from dollar strength and a +0.48pp 1-month jump in the 10y real yield, and added uncertainty from the CFO transition ahead of Q3 results (research/EOG/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Bear case; research/EOG/2026-10-08-macro.md macro_tilt).

target_price_12m.cite: research/EOG/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Decision JSON scenarios.bear.target_price_12m=119, basis: P/E falls back to 5y minimum of 9.3x on TTM EPS

target_band.cite: Half the spread between bear-case implied prices from three valuation anchors at TTM fundamentals: P/E fall to 5y min 9.3x = $118.69, P/FCF fall to 5y min 10.5x = $132.83, EV/EBITDA fall to 5y min 5.3x = $138.74 (fact sheet 5y multiple ranges, research/EOG/factsheet-2026-10-08.md Valuation table); half-spread $10.02 / $119 target = 0.084.

expected_12m_move.cite: Mixed factor_news for SPY (research/EOG/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json factor_news.SPY): record highs and $1tn combined SPY/SPYM assets (ETF Trends, Bloomberg, CNBC 2026-10-06/07) set against tech-led gains masking a broader sell-off, elevated Treasury yields pressuring stocks, and a large bearish put-spread trade (TipRanks, Reuters, WSJ, CNBC 2026-10-07); no net directional view supported, so 0.

factor_news for IEF (research/EOG/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json factor_news.IEF) is dominated by rising-yield/falling-bond-price headlines: '30-Year Yields Return to 2002 High', 'Global Bond Markets Sell Off on France's Fiscal Worries', 'Bond Rout Is Deepening', 'US Benchmark 10-Year Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002' (Bloomberg/Barrons/WSJ, 2026-10-01 to 10-07), only partly offset by brief rebounds (ETF Trends, Guardian, Bloomberg 2026-10-02); consistent with the macro overlay's cited DFII10 +0.48pp/1m and DGS10 +0.49pp/1m rise (research/EOG/2026-10-08-macro.md market_pricing), which implies lower bond prices. Modest negative move, within the ±15% guard.

jumps.name: Earnings surprise (quarterly release)
jumps.reason: EOG's revenue and earnings are driven each quarter by realized oil/gas volumes and prices; the next release is Q3 2026 on Nov 5, 2026, and the analogue history shows earnings weeks can move the stock sharply in either direction. Earnings occur every quarter, so a reporting event is certain within the 12m horizon.
jumps.cite: research/EOG/factsheet-2026-10-08.md Price section 'Next earnings date Nov 5, 2026 (Earnings Date)'; research/EOG/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks earnings_release entries

annual_probability.cite: Quarterly reporting cadence means at least one earnings-driven move is certain within the 12m horizon; research/EOG/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks lists 4 earnings_release weeks per year, so probability of an earnings-week shock occurring in the year is 1.

impact.cite: Largest adverse earnings-week move in the 5y analogue history: Q2 2026 release week, research/EOG/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks entry week 2026-08-03, move -0.0938.

jumps.reason: Ann Janssen's retirement and Jeff Hibbard's appointment as incoming CFO (announced 2026-09-24); his first full quarter (Q3 2026, reported ~Nov 5-6, 2026) is flagged as a watch point for any change in capital-allocation tone.
